overview:
California's second district covers the North Coast and leans strongly Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about thirteen points. Incumbent Jared Huffman is running again and carries more than one million dollars in cash on hand. His Republican opponent, Robin Littau, shows no reported fundraising or cash, and no outside groups have spent money in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the incumbent's financial edge. Prediction markets price Huffman's chances at about ninety-eight percent, in line with the district's history of double-digit Democratic margins. The forecast places Huffman well ahead, with a comfortable expected margin and low odds of an upset, while allowing some uncertainty given the absence of direct polling in the general election.
